_doc: Labelled sample PR diffs encoding the core-store schema migration
convention (migrations/README.md). Each fixture is a real unified diff
against this repo's current src DDL — they apply cleanly with
`git apply --check` from the repo root — and `expect` is the verdict the
schema-migration audit gate (landing separately) must produce for a PR
with that diff:
pass — the gate exits 0 (additive change, artifact shipped, or the
touched DDL is out of scope: Better Auth / extension-owned)
fail — the gate exits non-zero (destructive in-scope change with no
migrations/core/core__NNNN_*.mjs runner module + per-migration
manifest fragment migrations/manifest.d/core__NNNN_*.json in
the same diff — the legacy migrations/NNNN_*.sql psql form is
retired for new migrations and also fails, and appending to the
frozen migrations/manifest.json array fails too)
The pinned base a fixture replays against is base-manifest.json (the
frozen legacy array snapshot, max seq 0012) + base-manifest.d/ (the
shipped-fragment snapshot: seq 0014, leaving 0013 a deliberate gap for
the non-monotonic fixture).
The gate's classifier test must run every fixture and assert its label.
When the convention gains a new destructive/additive case, add a fixture
here in the same PR that documents it.

fixtures.description: Drops usage_events.agent_label (CREATE-DDL text, legacy DO-block adds, and an inline DROP COLUMN) without shipping a migrations/ artifact.

Narrows usage_events.cost_usd numeric(12,8) -> numeric(12,4) and ships the node-pg-migrate runner module migrations/core/core__0015_narrow-usage-events-cost-usd.mjs plus its per-migration manifest fragment migrations/manifest.d/core__0015_narrow-usage-events-cost-usd.json in the same diff (the fragment authoring form adopted in cinatra#1335; seq 0015 > the max shipped base seq 0014).

Same retype + runner module, but the ledger entry is APPENDED to the legacy migrations/manifest.json array instead of authored as a fragment. The legacy array is frozen shipped history (cinatra#1335) — the shared positional tail was the merge hotspot — so the gate rejects the append and points at migrations/manifest.d/.

fixtures.category: fragment double-claim (duplicate seq within the diff)
fixtures.description: Two module+fragment pairs both claim seq 0015 under different slugs — the double-claim collision class from the cinatra#1335 ledger. Module-aligned fragment names mean the two PRs add DIFFERENT paths (no git add/add conflict); merged together the union gate reds deterministically on the duplicate seq instead of misreading shipped history.

A fragment (plus module) re-claims seq 0012, which is already shipped in the frozen legacy array. The union never dedupes across forms — a seq present in both the legacy array and a fragment is a hard error.

A fragment (plus module) claims seq 0013 — unique over the union (0013 is a gap) but NOT strictly greater than the max shipped base seq (fragment 0014 in the pinned base-manifest.d/). Monotonicity over the union is what keeps a seq below an already-deployed ledger head from ever landing; this also proves the gate enumerates the BASE manifest.d/ directory, not just diff-touched paths.

Rewrites the summary of the shipped pinned fragment migrations/manifest.d/core__0014_pinned-shipped-fragment.json. A shipped fragment is immutable ledger history — editing, deleting, or renaming it is tampering, exactly like rewriting a legacy array entry.
Adds migrations/manifest.d/NOTES.txt. Malformed or unrecognized files under manifest.d/ are errors, not skips — every consumer's union read refuses them, so the gate stops them at the PR.

Same cost_usd retype but shipping the RETIRED legacy psql artifact (migrations/0012_*.sql + manifest entry). The core runner never executes loose .sql files, so the gate rejects the form and demands a migrations/core/core__NNNN_*.mjs module.

Adds a VALID migrations/core/core__0005_*.mjs module carrying destructive SQL with no manifest entry and no in-scope schema-file diff. The runner executes every valid core/ module regardless of the manifest, so migration-state inconsistency must fail standalone — not only when a destructive drizzle-store diff is present.

Edits migrations/manifest.json _doc wording without touching the migrations array. Legitimate without a module — the standalone inconsistency rule fires only when the array GAINS entries with no matching module (rewrites/removals of existing entries are integrity failures via the append-only prefix check).
Adds a nullable agent_templates.icon column (ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS) and a partial index — no data impact, no artifact required.
Removes a Better Auth additional user field (destructive-shaped, but auth schema is owned by getMigrations and guarded by auth-schema-drift); the gate must ignore it.

fixtures.category: out of scope (extension DDL), bundled with in-scope additive
fixtures.description: Adds destructive-shaped extension-owned SQL (a DROP COLUMN example in the extension migration host, the #118 out-of-scope surface) bundled with an in-scope additive index; the out-of-scope hunks must not trip the gate. Refreshed in #118 when the JSON-DSL files it originally touched were retired.
